Hello folks,

I am new to the community, I am trying to create consumer bindings for the input and GPIO APIs. I have a fair share of experience binding C APIs in userspace and I am trying to accomodate myself to how bindings works in the kernel.

Something that is confusing me, or even rubbing me off the wrong way, is that the pattern seems to be that bindings consume bindgen's as the canonical source for public struct mappings.

However, this creates a runtime burden to safely wrap each field, say you have a nullable const char*, by setting it as Option<&'static CStr> you let the type system and the compiler deal with safe assignments and checks, instead we have to wrap everything around getters/setters that add to code size and requires a closer look to make sure we get right.

I was wondering if this is something that has been discussed before to udnerstand where the community is at around this topic, I wonder if I should entertain the idea of adding some sort of override system for bindgen or annotations as comments.

Any feedback and guidance around this is welcome, thank you!
If you can't guarantee invariants at compile time through the type system, you must add a runtime check.
Just to take your example, having bindgen output Option<&CStr> for a field that is const char * on the c-side wouldn't work because said Rust type also contains the length of the string.

Unless you are just writing for fun and learning, you might want to do a search on lore.com. There was recently some GPIO consumer stuff posted: https://lore.kernel.org/rust-for-linux/20260906-add-rust-gpio-consumer-v1-0-24d192f93760@gmail.com/
Ah, thanks for the pointer to the GPIO stuff!

For now I am just trying to understand if I can help with binding coverage, I saw no binding for GPIO and assumed no one was working on it, great.

I am focusing on input at the moment.

Alice Ryhl said:

Just to take your example, having bindgen output Option<&CStr> for a field that is const char * on the c-side wouldn't work because said Rust type also contains the length of the string.

But the size information does not get mapped to repr(c), I am not sure I understand why that would be an issue
In any case, my assumption that I am expected to use the C type mappings generated by bindgen is correct right?
Yes, you should avoid providing your own.
(There are definitely things that can be improved in bindgen, i.e. this is not to say the generated bindings are perfect or optimal, but in that case we should improve the tool)
Also, I am not sure I follow how that Option would be safe. Even if the pointer is non-NULL, it may still be invalid.

Sure but it reflects nullability and enforces checks, I find the current pointer marshalling inside getter setters is potentially more fragile as you need to write the marshalling code manually and ensure its written and maintained to be correct. All that work is done by the type system anyhow if the struct binding had a higher level type than the raw pointer.

None of this fixes the problem of an invalid pointer though, but you'd need to transmute an invalid pointer to a Some(&'static CStr) to enforce that situation.
Anyway, I don't want to bikeshed, I just wanted to check if this is something that was discussed before to know how to go ahead with my binding, that's all.
The other problem it'd solve is that you could populate a new instance of the struct without calling into all those setter methods.
